title: The closure of the diagonal is a common dense refinement
statement:
Let $S$ be qcqs, let $f:X\to S$ be separated of finite type, and let
$c_k=(X\xrightarrow{j_k}\overline X_k\xrightarrow{p_k}S)$, $k=1,2$, be
compactifications of $f$. Let $Z$ be the scheme-theoretic image of

$$
\delta=(j_1,j_2):X\longrightarrow P:=\overline X_1\times_S\overline X_2 ,
$$

with projections $q_k:Z\to\overline X_k$. Then $\delta$ factors as a
quasi-compact, scheme-theoretically dense open immersion $j:X\to Z$ followed
by the closed immersion $Z\hookrightarrow P$; the structure map $Z\to S$ is
proper, so $c=(X\xrightarrow{j}Z\to S)$ is a dense compactification; and
each $q_k$ is a refinement $c\to c_k$ in the sense of
[det-nagata-definition-refinement], i.e. $q_kj=j_k$ and
$q_k^{-1}(j_k(X))=j(X)$.

Consequently every finite nonempty family of compactifications of $f$ has a
common dense refinement.

proof.text: Use the proved upstream graph-image construction Compactification.inf from WeilConjectures.Compactification.CommonRefinement. Its fields and the lemmas inf_Z, inf_i, infFst_hom and infSnd_hom give the specified scheme, maps, properness and openness; Hom.toImage_imageι gives the factorization. Category.assoc gives the stated structure-map formula. Compactification.quasiCompact_openImmersion gives quasi-compactness for every compactification occurring here.

proof.text: Use Compactification.isSchemeTheoreticallyDominant_inf_i: the open map is the canonical map to the scheme-theoretic image, so its sheaf-map kernel is zero. This applies without density assumptions on the input compactifications.

proof.text: The proved upstream isPullback_infFst and isPullback_infSnd identify the two open squares as cartesian. Apply range_snd_of_isPullback to each flipped square. Equality of the resulting underlying open sets gives equality in Scheme.Opens by SetLike.coe_injective. These are exactly the two boundaryRefinementProperty assertions; the triangle equalities already belong to infFst and infSnd.

proof.text: For a finite family d, induct on finite subsets of its index type. Start with the dense compactification inf c₁ c₁ and no required projections, using the c₁ already provided by the theorem, so no unconditional empty-family existence is assumed. For insertion of i, replace a previously obtained e by inf e (d i). The second projection handles i. Compose the first projection with every preceding refinement r; Refinement.comp gives both triangles, and Hom.comp_preimage followed by the two boundary equalities proves preservation of the distinguished open. Finally use the universal finite subset. This proves the required nonempty finite-family conclusion, including non-dense singleton families.
